ai.headline: Lyft adds inferences, expands location-specific privacy rights, and raises its children's age limit to 16
ai.summary: Lyft now says it may infer things about you from your rides and information, such as whether you are a frequent traveler or your gender from your first name. It also extends state-specific privacy rights to more places (Canada, Montana, Oregon, and Texas added), and raises the age under which it does not knowingly collect personal information from children from 13 to 16. Lyft also removed its statement that it may infer information from your use, and it reworded many "sharing" sections as "disclosing," with the sharing of data for personalized ads now described as going to third parties only.

ai.headline: Lyft adds Family accounts, rewards data, and age checks to its privacy policy
ai.summary: Lyft's updated privacy policy adds Lyft Family accounts and rewards points balances to the information it may share or track, and says it may use people's age to verify their identity. It also adds an on-device location feature that only sends Lyft your location if you tap a notification, and it expands the list of states with specific privacy rights. Several other changes are wording updates, such as adding bankruptcy to the list of business transactions where data may be shared and saying Lyft will seek consent where required by law.
